newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas extends gains on colder forecast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas extends gains on colder forecast.

text.p: U.S. spot gas prices rose further Tuesday as cold temperatures continued in the central U.S. and forecasts called for the arrival of below-normal temperatures in the Northeast by week's end, sources said.
Swing prices on the Gulf Coast pipes climbed by about five cents to the low-$3 per mmBtu area. Freezing temperatures seeped into northern Texas today, attracting more spot buyers to the marketplace.
Early February bidweek prices were talked in the low-to-mid $2.90s, about a $1 under January indices.
In the Midcontinent, where temperatures are at least 10 degrees below normal, prices gained more than five cents to about $3.
Early February prices on the Midcontinent pipes were talked around $2.80, with Demarcation quoted at $2.90.
Temperatures in the Midwest in the first week of February are expected to return to normal to above-normal levels.
In west Texas, Permian next-day prices were up another eight cents to the $2.89-2.94 range, while the Waha market climbed into the $2.95-3.00 area.
Prices at the southern California border rose by more than five cents to the $2.94-2.99 range. February 1 prices at the border were talked in the low-to-mid $2.60s.

Southern California Edison said again that its 1,070 megawatt San Onofre nuclear power unit will likely return to service about two weeks later than the originally scheduled restart date of February 8.
In the East, prices at the New York city-gate firmed by about 20 cents to the $3.55-3.70 range. Similar prices were talked for February 1 delivery.
